$schema-note: Canonical registry of Owlette web env vars. KEYS + metadata only — values NEVER live here, they stay in the providers. Edit this file when you add/remove/move an env var, then run `node scripts/sync-env.mjs check`. See .claude/skills/env-management.md.

classes.public: NEXT_PUBLIC_* — inlined into the client bundle at build time; not secret. Synced non-sensitive so values stay readable in Vercel.
classes.config: Non-secret app configuration (emails, ids, endpoints, flags). Synced non-sensitive.
classes.must-match: Sensitive AND silently catastrophic if it differs between mirror targets: SESSION_SECRET logs everyone out, MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY locks out 2FA users, LLM_ENCRYPTION_KEY breaks stored Cortex keys. Synced --sensitive.

never-set.$note: Env vars the web code reads that must NEVER exist on railway-dev, railway-prod, or vercel-prod. They are inventoried here and deliberately kept OUT of `vars` below — that omission IS the guard. `sync-env.mjs` computes `undeclared` as live keys minus `manifest.vars` without regard to `targets`, so an unregistered key that turns up on a target is reported as drift and `check` exits 1. Registering one under `vars` — even with an empty `targets` — would permanently silence that alarm. These belong in a local `.env.local` or a Playwright `webServer.env` only. This block is documentation: `sync-env.mjs` reads `targets`, `mirror`, and `vars`, and ignores everything else.

keys.ALLOW_INSECURE_WEBHOOK_URLS: '1' drops the https-only requirement on user-supplied webhook endpoints (web/lib/webhookUrl.ts:25), downgrading an SSRF guard. Local-dev http smoke tests only. Captured at module scope, so it only takes effect at process start.
keys.E2E_DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT: 'true' turns both rate limiters into an unconditional allow (web/lib/rateLimit.ts:376, web/lib/rateLimit.server.ts:535) and suppresses the production boot alarm for a missing distributed limiter (web/instrumentation.ts:20). Injected only by the Playwright webServer env (web/playwright.config.ts:156).
keys.ENABLE_CAPABILITY_ENFORCEMENT: Firestore-outage fallback only — the live switch is the `global/security_config` document (docs/runbooks/security-boundary-kill-switches.md). Unset means enabled (web/lib/securityConfig.server.ts:94-98 is fail-safe); setting 'false' would disable capability checks fleet-wide during any Firestore blip.
keys.ENABLE_RATE_LIMIT_ENFORCEMENT: Same Firestore-outage fallback as ENABLE_CAPABILITY_ENFORCEMENT, governing rate-limit enforcement (web/lib/securityConfig.server.ts:112). Unset means enabled.
keys.FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST: Presence alone — any value — flips the Admin SDK into emulator mode, initializing without a service-account credential (web/lib/firebase-admin.ts:37-41). On a deploy target every server-side read and write would silently leave production Firestore. Set only by the Playwright emulator runner.
keys.FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST: Second trigger for the same Admin SDK emulator branch (web/lib/firebase-admin.ts:39) — either variable alone is sufficient, so both must stay absent.
keys.GCLOUD_PROJECT: Runtime-injected inside GCP, never on Railway or Vercel. Read only as a fallback for the audit-log project id (web/lib/auditLogClient.ts:34), which FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID already satisfies on all three targets. Same do-not-sync rule as RAILWAY_*.
keys.LEGACY_API_KEY_ALLOW_HASH_LIST: Companion allowlist of SHA-256 key hashes for LEGACY_API_KEY_BYPASS_ENABLED (web/lib/apiAuth.server.ts:66) — inert alone, dangerous paired.
keys.LEGACY_API_KEY_BYPASS_ENABLED: 'true' re-admits pre-scope-system API keys with empty or missing scopes (web/lib/apiAuth.server.ts:65). Shipped as an emergency-only migration hatch (docs/runbooks/upgrade-2.12.0.md).
keys.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST: Browser-side auth emulator host, applied only when NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_FIREBASE_EMULATOR is 'true' (web/lib/firebase.ts:79). NEXT_PUBLIC_ vars are inlined at build time, so it must be absent from the build environment, not just the runtime one.
keys.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_EMULATOR_HO: Browser-side storage emulator host — same gate and same build-time inlining as NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST (web/lib/firebase.ts:89).
keys.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST: Browser-side Firestore emulator host — same gate and same build-time inlining as NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST (web/lib/firebase.ts:84).
keys.NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_FIREBASE_EMULATOR: 'true' points the browser Firebase SDK at localhost emulators (web/lib/firebase.ts:31, :74) and skips App Check init (web/lib/firebase.ts:128). On a deploy target it takes the dashboard down for every visitor, and because it is NEXT_PUBLIC_ it is baked into the bundle at build time — unsetting it later does not undo a build that saw it. Injected only by the Playwright webServer env.
keys.OWLETTE_E2E: '1' swaps the real R2 object store for Firestore-backed stand-ins (web/lib/r2Client.server.ts:151, :243, :305) and changes installer-upload behaviour (web/app/api/installer/upload/route.ts:44). On a deploy target it would silently disconnect roost uploads from R2. Injected only by the Playwright webServer env (web/playwright.config.ts:163).

AUDIT_LOG_REGION.note: optional override — defaults to us-central1, which is where recordAuditEvent deploys (functions/src/auditLog.ts:193 declares no region). Set only if the function moves region

AUDIT_LOG_URL.note: optional override — the recordAuditEvent url is otherwise composed from FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID + AUDIT_LOG_REGION (web/lib/auditLogClient.ts:29-38), which already resolves on all three targets

CLOUDFLARE_TURN_KEY_API_TOKEN.note: bearer that mints swoop ICE credentials at rtc.live.cloudflare.com. It cannot query the GraphQL analytics API — TURN usage metering needs its own token

FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET.note: server-side fallback after NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET (web/lib/screenshotStorage.server.ts:51-53, screenshots/finalize/route.ts:83-85) — never fires while the NEXT_PUBLIC_ variant is set on all three targets

INSTATUS_API_BASE_URL.note: optional override — defaults to https://api.instatus.com (web/lib/instatusClient.ts:61). Set only to point at a mock or a non-default Instatus host

INSTATUS_COMPONENT_AGENT_REGISTRY_ID.note: required status-page component — read dynamically via INSTATUS_COMPONENT_ENV (web/lib/instatusClient.ts:52-56), so it never greps as a literal process.env read. Unset on every target today, so status-ping skips it and validateInstatusConfig reports the page unconfigured. Belongs on railway-prod + vercel-prod alongside INSTATUS_COMPONENT_DASHBOARD_ID — promote once the Instatus component exists

INSTATUS_COMPONENT_ALERT_DELIVERY_ID.note: optional status-page component — alert_delivery's primary channel is Sentry, so a missing id must not fail validateInstatusConfig or the readiness gate (web/lib/instatusClient.ts:47, scripts/check-status-page-ready.mjs:38). Promote only if an Instatus component is created for it

INSTATUS_COMPONENT_API_ID.note: required status-page component — same dynamic read path and same promotion rule as INSTATUS_COMPONENT_AGENT_REGISTRY_ID

INSTATUS_COMPONENT_CORTEX_CHAT_ID.note: required status-page component for the hoot chat surface — the env name keeps the wire-level `cortex` spelling on purpose (web/lib/instatusClient.ts:41). Same promotion rule as INSTATUS_COMPONENT_AGENT_REGISTRY_ID

INSTATUS_COMPONENT_FIRESTORE_ID.note: required status-page component — same dynamic read path and same promotion rule as INSTATUS_COMPONENT_AGENT_REGISTRY_ID

INSTATUS_COMPONENT_R2_UPLOADS_ID.note: required status-page component — same dynamic read path and same promotion rule as INSTATUS_COMPONENT_AGENT_REGISTRY_ID

INSTATUS_COMPONENT_STATUS_METHOD.note: optional override — defaults to PUT (web/lib/instatusClient.ts:62); must be PUT, PATCH, or POST (scripts/check-status-page-ready.mjs:152)

INSTATUS_COMPONENT_STATUS_URL_TEMPLATE.note: optional override carrying {pageId} + {componentId} placeholders — empty selects the built-in /v2/{pageId}/components/{componentId} path on the api base url (web/lib/instatusClient.ts:108)

INSTATUS_COMPONENT_TALON_DISPATCH_ID.note: optional status-page component — exempt from the readiness gate for the same reason as INSTATUS_COMPONENT_ALERT_DELIVERY_ID (web/lib/instatusClient.ts:47, scripts/check-status-page-ready.mjs:38)

INSTATUS_COMPONENT_WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_ID.note: required status-page component — same dynamic read path and same promotion rule as INSTATUS_COMPONENT_AGENT_REGISTRY_ID

LLM_ENCRYPTION_KEY.note: mismatch between railway-prod and vercel-prod breaks decryption of stored LLM provider keys

MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY.note: mismatch locks out every 2FA user on failover — values must be byte-identical across mirror targets

NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL.note: stray alias — its only read is the health-check base-url fallback (web/lib/healthChecks.server.ts:55). NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is the canonical public origin, so prefer deleting that read over setting this

NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APPCHECK_SITE_KEY.note: App Check stays inert until this reCAPTCHA Enterprise site key is set (web/lib/firebase.ts:126) and is always skipped against the emulator. Deliberately deferred — move to all three targets during the rollout (docs/runbooks/app-check-rollout.md:63,146), not before

NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY.note: sitekey is public by design (rendered in the page). One widget covers owlette.app, dev.owlette.app, localhost, 127.0.0.1 — same value everywhere

OWLETTE_STATUS_BASE_URL.note: optional override for the origin the synthetic health checks probe — the RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN rung of the fallback chain (web/lib/healthChecks.server.ts:52-57) already resolves on both Railway services

RATE_LIMIT_OBSERVE_ONLY.note: dev-only — rate limiting runs in observe (non-blocking) mode

SEND_WELCOME_EMAIL.note: opt-in — only the exact string 'true' sends a welcome email on signup (web/app/api/webhooks/user-created/route.ts:82); documented default is false

SESSION_SECRET.note: mismatch invalidates every session cookie on failover — all users logged out

SWOOP_JWT_KID.note: key id stamped into every swoop JWT header; the signaling worker accepts two active public keys so rotation is not a flag day

SWOOP_JWT_KID_PREVIOUS.note: key id of SWOOP_JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_PREVIOUS. rotate the worker first, then the api, or tokens minted under the new kid 401 at the relay

SWOOP_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY.note: EdDSA signing key for swoop viewer/host/doorbell tokens — if railway-prod and vercel-prod differ, every token minted by the failover origin fails verification at the signaling worker

SWOOP_JWT_PUBLIC_KEY.note: verification half of SWOOP_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY — public by design, and also configured on the signaling worker

SWOOP_JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_PREVIOUS.note: the retiring public key during a kid rotation. PROTOCOL.md §11 requires every bundle to carry two active keys so a rotation is not a flag day; unset outside a rotation window

SWOOP_SESSION_MASTER_KEY.note: root of the per-viewer key derivation (K_session = HKDF(key, sid)) — a mismatch across the mirror silently breaks every key a failover-minted session derived

SWOOP_SIGNAL_RING_SECRET.note: shared secret on POST /v1/ring — a ring from the failover origin 401s against a worker holding railway-prod's value, intermittently and invisibly

SWOOP_SIGNAL_URL.note: signaling worker origin. Returned to the browser by the session-create route, never as a NEXT_PUBLIC_ var, and the source of the swoop connect-src entry in web/proxy.ts

TURNSTILE_HOSTNAMES.note: per-deployment frontend hostname allowlist checked against the siteverify response — dev: dev.owlette.app, prod: owlette.app. NEVER include localhost in a prod value

TURNSTILE_SECRET.note: one Turnstile widget serves both origins, so railway-prod and vercel-prod must match or failover breaks register + forgot-password

W8_1_DRILL_TS.note: temporary security-drill marker (wave 8.1) — remove from Railway + this manifest when the drill is retired
